newsitem.title: pakistan: Gas spillage kills 26 in Pakistan's Lahore.
newsitem.headline: Gas spillage kills 26 in Pakistan's Lahore.

text.p: A leakage of poisonous gas from a tanker truck killed 26 people and sickened more than 900 in the Pakistani city of Lahore, hospital doctors said on Thursday.

More than 900 people were taken to various hospitals after the gas, which doctors said was ammonia, leaked from cylinders being carried on a truck through Lahore's populous Mughalpura district on Wednesday night.
Most of the victims were given first aid and allowed to go home, but more than 150 were still in hospitals, some of them in critical condition, the doctors said.
There was confusion about the type of gas, which also killed many animals, including buffalo, which was being carried to a factory making jeans.
Doctors said it was ammonia, while local administration chief, deputy commissioner Kamran Lashari, said he thought it was chlorine.
The official APP news agency quoted sources in the chemical department of the Punjab University as saying the gas might have been choloroquine, which can cause hypoxia and spasms.
"People started rushing out of their houses choking," a witness said, describing scenes of panic. "Some fell unconscious and nobody was in a position to help the other."
Reporters who toured the area said the gas had largely dispersed, although an acrid smell remained.
Police and troops patrolled the streets in gas masks and the bodies of many animals and chickens lay where they had choked to death, they said.
Cries of mourning could be heard from many houses in the area, while many people searched for their children and other relatives who had been removed from their homes by rescuers.
"There is mourning in the whole area," Mohammad Anwar, a local resident, said.
After the incident, the army took control and launched a relief operation. The fire brigade and civil rescue workers also rushed to the scene to help hundreds of affected residents, APP said.
The provincial government announced compensation of 50,000 rupees ($1,243) for each dead person.
